source_name: Portalb.mk — Albanian-language MK news portal (Metamorphosis Foundation)
why_relevant: Principal Albanian-language MK outlet; covers NBRM warnings on merchant unwillingness to accept electronic payments — acceptance-side intelligence largely absent from MK-language reporting, and covers western-MK (Tetovo/Gostivar/Struga) branch and ATM realities. Fact-checking pedigree raises reliability.

source_name: Alsat TV (alsat.mk) — Ekonomi section
why_relevant: Bilingual MK/Albanian broadcaster; broke fintech licensing news (Flex Pay receiving an e-money institution licence from the National Bank) and covers electronic tolling/payment-acceptance changes — new-entrant and acceptance-channel intelligence.

source_name: Telegrafi — Maqedoni / Ekonomi verticals (Kosovo outlet covering MK)
why_relevant: Largest Albanian-language regional portal with a dedicated North Macedonia economy vertical and a bank-card topic tag (kartelat bankare); gives regional comparative framing (KS/AL/MK) and reaches MK Albanian audiences.

source_name: Almakos.com — Albanian-language MK portal
why_relevant: Carries bank marketing/promotional campaigns in MK (e.g. UNI Banka x Mastercard “Paguaj dhe hyr në lojë”), which are a cheap proxy for card-issuer competitive pushes and scheme partnerships in the Albanian-speaking segment.

source_name: TIME.mk — Macedonian news aggregator
why_relevant: The canonical MK news aggregator, indexing essentially all relevant MK outlets with per-source pages (e.g. time.mk/s/biznisinfo) and an Economy category. Best single discovery surface for outlets this cell has not yet enumerated, and a cheap way to detect when a payments story goes multi-outlet. Headlines+snippets only, so it is a pointer, not a content source.

source_name: GRID.mk — competing Macedonian news aggregator
why_relevant: Second MK aggregator; different source list and ranking than TIME.mk, so it surfaces smaller/regional outlets TIME may de-prioritise. Redundancy for discovery if TIME.mk blocks automated access.

source_name: AAG — ranking of most-read web portals in North Macedonia
why_relevant: Audience-measurement style listing of the most-read MK web portals: lets this cell prioritise media monitoring by reach rather than guesswork, and enumerates outlets not yet in the source register.

source_name: Bankometar.mk — MK bank product comparison portal
why_relevant: Not a newsroom but a media-adjacent comparison site enumerating debit/credit card products across MK banks; effectively a structured, continuously updated snapshot of the card issuing landscape and pricing — a strong cross-check on media claims about fees and product launches.

source_name: Vrabotuvanje.com.mk — national job portal (banking & IT categories)
why_relevant: Largest general MK job board; banks (NLB, Komercijalna, Sparkasse, Halkbank) post IT and payments roles here. Ads specify platforms, integrations and project scope ('развој, имплементација и поддршка на ИТ решенија и платформи'), an early indicator of core-banking/card-platform projects. Portal also runs banking-news items (e.g. NBRSM payment-services bylaws).

source_name: KARIERA.mk — job portal, company profile pages
why_relevant: Second major MK job board with per-company pages (e.g. Nextsense) that expose employer hiring history — useful for tracking payments vendors and PSPs, not only banks. Search endpoint at /search allows role-keyword monitoring.

source_name: e-Rabota — Employment Agency of RNM official vacancy register
why_relevant: State register of active vacancies; employers including banks are legally routed through the Agency. Gives an authoritative, low-noise baseline of who is hiring and in which occupational category, and covers employers that never advertise on commercial boards.

source_name: Pazar3.mk — jobs/business classifieds
why_relevant: High-traffic MK classifieds carrying lower-tier vacancies — merchant-side POS support, field technicians, agent networks — that rarely appear on bank career pages. Weak but genuinely complementary signal on acquiring/field-service capacity.

source_name: Joberty — MK IT employer profiles (incl. CaSys / Интернационален Картичен Систем)
why_relevant: Developer-review/employer platform with a dedicated profile for CaSys, the national card processor — tech-stack mentions, review text and openings reveal what platforms the processor actually runs and how it is staffing. Rare visibility into a normally opaque actor.

source_name: KIBS AD — LinkedIn company page
why_relevant: KIBS is the interbank clearing operator for small-value payments and the first MK certificate authority. Its LinkedIn posts and job ads are the earliest public trace of SEPA readiness, instant-payment scheme work and PKI/e-ID projects.

source_name: Komercijalna Banka AD — LinkedIn company page (vacancy posts)
why_relevant: The largest MK bank posts full vacancy texts to LinkedIn ('ОГЛАС ЗА ВРАБОТУВАЊЕ: Двајца стручни…'), naming the organisational unit. Same pattern applies to NLB, Stopanska, Halkbank, Sparkasse, ProCredit — a bank-by-bank LinkedIn watchlist is the core of this cell.

source_name: Nextsense — LinkedIn / company careers (MK payments & e-ID vendor)
why_relevant: MK software vendor delivering digital-identity, remote-signing and e-invoicing to MK banks (co-developer of OneID with KIBS). Its hiring and product posts flag which bank-side digital projects are live before any bank announces them.

source_name: Regional E-commerce Conference Skopje (AETM / ecommerce.mk)
why_relevant: Flagship annual MK e-commerce gathering (9th edition, November) with a dedicated payments/fintech track. The agenda and speaker list identify who runs card-not-present acquiring, PSP integrations and 3-D Secure/SCA rollouts on the merchant side. Organiser AETM (ecommerce.mk) also publishes explainer content on KIBS digital certificates.

source_name: Balkan Payment Forum (Promoney Events)
why_relevant: Regional payments conference whose speaker roster includes MK actors (e.g. the founder of Paysera Macedonia) alongside Eurosystem market-infrastructure officials. Agenda topics track what regional regulators and PSPs consider live — SEPA accession, instant payments, licensing.

source_name: Macedonian Banking Association (МБА) — commissions and events
why_relevant: The MBA runs a standing Commission for Payment Cards and Digital Banking chaired by named executives from Stopanska, Komercijalna and NLB. That membership list is the single best public map of who owns cards/payments strategy at each MK bank, and MBA statements (e.g. SCA go-live from 1 March 2026) pre-announce scheme-level changes.

source_name: IT.mk — MK tech media, events and IT-careers section
why_relevant: Covers MK tech events (e.g. Skopje Hackathon – Blockchain+AI edition) and carries an IT jobs section. Useful for catching fintech hackathons, vendor hiring waves and event announcements that never reach banking-specific media.

source_name: Skopje Blockchain Summit & Hackathon (Base42 venue ecosystem)
why_relevant: Recurring Skopje hackathon/summit (48h, Base42) drawing regional fintech builders and sponsors. Sponsor lists and challenge briefs occasionally come from banks/PSPs and reveal which institutions are experimenting with open banking, tokenisation or crypto rails.

source_name: NBRSM — research work and economic publications (Истражувачка работа)
why_relevant: The central bank publishes working papers and analytical notes alongside its payment-systems section. For this cell the value is the authorship layer: NBRSM working papers on cash usage, payment habits and card acceptance identify in-house researchers and methodologies that later surface at conferences. Also hosts the National Payment Systems Council pages, which name the institutional participants.

source_name: UKIM institutional repository (Ss. Cyril and Methodius University, Skopje)
why_relevant: Master's and doctoral theses from the Faculty of Economics and FINKI frequently use primary MK card/POS/ATM data obtained from banks or NBRSM and reproduce it in appendices — sometimes the only public granular series. Supervisor and author names also map the domestic academic bench on payments.

source_name: Institute of Economics — UKIM (Економски институт)
why_relevant: Research institute supervising second-cycle economics theses and producing applied studies; a plausible host for MK-specific work on cash usage and financial inclusion, and a route to named domestic researchers.

source_name: Apliciraj.mk — employer-indexed vacancy aggregator (e.g. Halkbank AD Skopje)
why_relevant: Aggregator with per-employer pages listing all open positions at a given bank at once — a convenient per-institution hiring snapshot for Halkbank and peers, easier to diff over time than scattered career pages.

source_name: 'Бизнис лидер' conference (Makfax coverage) — fintech and innovation-financing panels
why_relevant: Domestic business conference whose 2025 edition carried a 'Fintech revolution and the future of finance' panel and an innovation-financing panel with named participants from Development Bank, Halkbank and academia. Panel rosters are a direct read on who is designated to speak for payments innovation at each institution.

source_name: НБРСМ — Ковани пари во оптек (coins in circulation)
why_relevant: Companion page to the banknote page; coin issue data completes the currency-in-circulation picture and signals low-value cash usage intensity.

source_name: НБРСМ — Годишна информација за движењата во плаќањата во Република Македонија (annual payments developments report)
why_relevant: Annual narrative-plus-data report on payment developments; historically the place where cash withdrawal volumes, ATM/POS counts and the cash-versus-card mix are presented together with commentary.
